newsitem.title: USA: California lawyer markets Heaven's Gate cult film.
newsitem.headline: California lawyer markets Heaven's Gate cult film.

text.p: A film made by the Heaven's Gate cult leaders 21 years ago, and which surfaced after the group's mass suicide in California, may be shown on television and released publicly on video.

A lawyer involved in marketing the film said on Sunday it outlined the genesis of the philosophy that ultimately led to the mass suicide in March of 39 cult members in San Diego, and only came to light a couple of weeks ago.
"We're working on getting it on a network TV news special," said Jerry Weinstein, of the Beverly Hills law firm Weinstein and Hart, who is working with the William Morris Agency.
Weinstein said the plan was to eventually release the film in video stores, as well.
The tape is believed to be the only authorised video featuring the cult's founders Marshall Applewhite and Bonnie Lu Nettles Trousdale explaining their philosophy.
The film was given to a midwestern producer 21 years ago in a deal requiring the producer to keep it under wraps until 30 days after their deaths.

Trousdale died in the mid-1980s but Applewhite carried on the vision until late March when he and 38 members killed themselves in a million-dollar mansion in north San Diego in the belief they would be taken away on a UFO hiding behind the Hale-Bopp comet.
Weinstein said he was contacted by the producer, who has requested anonymity, after the mass suicides.
"There are two hours worth of tapes," said Weinstein. "It's quite extensive."
